statement: Our production processes are designed to minimize environmental impact through efficient resource utilization, energy conservation, and responsible waste management.
All functional Departments work in cohesion to a common goal that includes utilizing natural resources with minimal or no damage to the environment and efficiency in energy.
Effluent treatment, waste heat recovery, and responsible waste disposal practices were further strengthened to minimize the environmental footprint.

The Company prioritizes waste minimization by optimizing production processes and encouraging the reuse and recycling of by-products within its operations to reduce the environmental and health impacts linked to hazardous waste.
The Company manages risks associated with legacy waste issues and the financial burden of environmental remediation and site restoration.

Iron ore and coal are essential inputs in steel manufacturing, yet their extraction can pose significant environmental and social challenges, affecting local communities, workers, and ecosystems.
The Company mitigates this risk by implementing water-efficient technologies, promoting water recycling and reuse within its operations, and ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.
Occupational Health, Safety & Environment Policy
The Company has obtained ISO 14001:2015 (Environmental Management Systems) for Kalwe and Hospet Factory.
Key initiatives include the implementation of modern regenerative combustion technologies, recycling of metal waste and treated water, and adoption of eco-friendly waste disposal methods.
The Company actively engages in environment-related awareness activities, such as tree plantation drives on World Environment Day and employee sensitization programs.
Installation of Multi-effect Evaporator for Zero Liquid Discharge, which helps in mitigating environmental impact on water resources.

By utilizing stainless steel scrap for the bulk of the material requirements, the Company significantly cut down on waste and mitigate the environmental impact associated with mining and processing raw materials.
At the company, all e-waste and hazardous waste are disposed of in an environmentally responsible manner through vendors approved by the Pollution Control Board.
The Company’s waste collection and management processes are fully aligned with the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) plan submitted to the relevant Pollution Control Boards.
The Company has adopted and implemented a comprehensive Occupational Health, Safety & Environment (OHSE) Policy across its Kalwe and Hospet units.
Due to the implementation of Zero Liquid Discharge mechanism in the Company, there is no water discharge.

The Company has integrated advanced water treatment solutions at its facility, including a Multi-Effect Evaporator (MEE) and an Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP), to ensure the effective management of all wastewater generated on-site.
The MEE system operates through multiple stages of evaporation to concentrate and significantly reduce the volume of effluent, thereby minimizing overall waste.
In parallel, the ETP is designed to treat and purify wastewater to meet stringent environmental standards, enabling safe reuse or responsible disposal.

The adoption of PNG significantly reduces emissions of carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and particulate matter, thereby supporting the Company’s broader objective of sustainable operations and environmental responsibility.
Spillage prevention and immediate cleanup procedures are implemented to avoid land contamination at the Kalwe Unit.
At the Hospet Unit, plastic waste is segregated and disposed of through authorized channels, ensuring minimal environmental impact.
At the Hospet Unit, obsolete electronic waste is systematically collected and stored in designated e-waste bins to prevent damage and contamination.

The Company is not currently operating in ecologically sensitive areas (such as national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, wetlands, biodiversity hotspots, forests, coastal regulation zones etc.).
The Company does not operate in environmentally fragile or ecologically sensitive areas.

Installed a Multi Effect Evaporator at the Effluent Treatment Plant to improve the quality of treated effluent from CFD and BBD processes, enabling 100% reuse of treated effluent within the process, significantly reducing freshwater consumption and minimizing effluent discharge impact on the environment at the Kalwe unit.

Minimized oil consumption from 0.14 L/MT to 0.10 L/MT by introducing an oil wiper system to limit oil carryover on bars at the BBD Kalwe unit, reducing oil usage and potential environmental contamination risks.
